subject: Quantitative Aptitude (QA)
exam_context: CAT 2026 - QA section only, 22 questions / 66 marks / 40 minutes
data_provenance: Estimated from a five-year (2021-2025, 15 slots, ~330 questions) PYQ weightage analysis and multiple slot-wise coaching trackers, not an official IIM-published weightage document; last grounded Sep 2026. Individual-slot weightage varies (e.g. CAT 2025 Slot 1 vs Slot 2 vs Slot 3 differ by 1-2 questions per topic), so treat as a multi-year, multi-slot average for question-bank planning.

Q01.notes: The single highest-weightage QA topic in every slot from 2021-2025 without exception; Averages/Ratios and Time-Speed-Distance/Work are the most consistently recurring sub-topics.

Q02.notes: Second-largest topic; quadratic equations, inequalities and functions/graphs are flagged as the toughest sub-topics across trackers.

Q03.notes: Steady presence every slot; questions often require an unfamiliar application of a familiar theorem rather than direct formula recall.

Q04.notes: Fewer questions than the top three topics but a reliable concept-tester; remainder-theorem and digit-based problems recur most.

Q05.notes: The most volatile topic in the five-year trend data - dropped to near-zero in some slots and spiked in others - so bank quotas should stay modest relative to the top three topics.

marking_scheme.source_note: Confirmed via multiple Sep 2026 sources reporting on the CAT 2025 (30 Nov 2025) session, consistent with the CAT 2024 pattern.
marking_scheme.mcq: +3 for a correct answer, -1 for an incorrect answer, 0 if unattempted.
marking_scheme.tita: +3 for a correct answer, 0 for an incorrect answer (no negative marking), 0 if unattempted.
marking_scheme.mcq_tita_split_typical: Approximately 14-17 MCQs and 5-8 TITA questions per slot.
marking_scheme.question_types_used: Single-correct MCQ and TITA (type-in-the-answer). No multiple-correct or matrix-match formats.
